[x-posting then elaborated from AskVoat 2] How do we make a 3rd political Party in America?

You could model the structure we use off of any of the countries that already have prominent third party groups.

Or you try going with an alternative vote, that way voting third party doesn't fuck with the results. The way we have it now is more or less that if you vote for a third party your vote goes out the window. If you would have voted for another candidate who had better chances, that candidate is now just out your vote. It's likely why you see so many of the media outlets that lean toward Clinton also giving Johnson love; he is far less likely to take votes away from Clinton and more likely to hurt Trump's chances. All Clinton has to do is get the most votes, not the majority. If the majority is split between two other candidates, their numbers would likely be lower than hers so blammo, presidency. Voting third party now may very well be the best way to elect the candidate you wanted in office least.

While the alternative vote isn't a perfect system either, it allows for people to rank their choices at the ballot instead of just picking one, meaning if their first choice loses, they still have a shot at electing the person they feel fits the spot best. This would free voters up to vote third party without the fear that they may just be taking votes away from someone else, making voting for a third party viable in a way it isn't currently.

Damage one of the existing parties beyond repair. And even then, I doubt it would create a viable third party. It would probably just create a new party that would supplant the old one. There are several reasons for this.

First, most elections in the US only require a plurality of votes to become elected. Second, when a person becomes elected, it's winner take all, as opposed to proportional representation. Both of these things cause political support in the United States to be incredibly partisan, and concentrated in specific geographic regions.

Duverger's law sums this up perfectly. Basically, if there's three political parties, it'll serve the interests of two parties to screw over the third party, even if they're ideological opposites.
For starters, we need four, not three. We currently have an authoritarian left and authoritarian right party; we need a libertarian left and libertarian right party.
Would a third part emerging cause a creation of a fourth party.

The big issue is you need to get rid of first past the post.

First past the post forces two parties. State representatives are the perfect example. Imagine a state has 100 representatives. And the state is divided perfectly evenly with 35% democrat, 30% republican, 20% libertarian, 15% green. What should their representatives be? Well most of everybody I think would say 35 democrats, 30 republicans, 20 libertarians, 15 greens. What are they instead? 100% democrat. How? We break the state up into tiny districts so we can force first past the post on it. The first district votes 35% democrat, 30% republican, etc - democrats win. And each other district follows suit. You end up with 100 democrats getting only 35% of the vote but 100% of the representation.

In order for a third party to exist in America, it needs to be more popular than both major parties. In other words, it can't exist. Proportional representation is the simple solution here. You have elections for state representatives at large. So that means everybody in the state votes for their representatives. If there are 20 seats then any party or individual that gets more than 5% of the vote is guaranteed at least one seat. A party gets 10% of the vote, they get at least 2 seats. Simple and fair. First past the post is the reason that fewer Americans than ever identify as democrat or republican, yet those two parties have control of nearly 100% of government seats - state and federal.

It's the really frustrating thing. First past the post seems so incredibly obviously fair, but it's not. I think if people understood what it causes and what it does - there'd be nationwide unified support for getting rid of it. But I tried to describe the issues as simply as I could here and it took two paragraphs and an example with a little bit of mathematic nuance. Whereas first past the post: "You get the most votes, you win. Fair!" One sentence that sounds completely reasonable, but actually is completely false.
